Scope: Independent controller-history Windows ACL / installer upgrade compatibility review
HashConvention: SHA256 complete bytes normalized CRLF to LF

Record.source: Installed r6 controller history; actual installer read-only admission

Executed.Provider: Actual Windows filesystem ACL Set/Get and actual installer Assert-Usb4StateHistory, elevated test session
Cases: New controller history protected and installer admitted
Legacy inherited private SYSTEM/Admin history sealed and installer admitted
Foreign history owner/grants refused with original ACL and custody bytes unchanged

Conclusions: Protection executes before history publication. Existing owner must be SYSTEM/Admin; every ACE must allow FullControl only to those SIDs and both grants must exist. Foreign ACLs fail before Set-Acl or state publication.
Private legacy history may be sealed; new history receives protected explicit SYSTEM/Admin inheritance and readback validation. No source downgrade, network or task operation added.
Current real-Windows controls detect the recorded installed r6 incompatibility rather than merely mocking protection flags.
Limits: Did not replay old-script staging/execution/deletion after the prior automatic policy rejection; load-bearing old-runtime evidence is the recorded read-only actual installed admission failure.
No live installed directory repair or controller/task deployment performed by this reviewer. Root retains responsibility for post-deployment readback.
Mutex/trusted-administrator assumptions remain; this does not establish atomic exclusion against arbitrary privileged ACL races.
